parameters.content:
## OPS - Capacity Ranker Campaign Watchdog

Every 5 minutes, 08:00–21:00 ET, Mon–Sat: GET LP-MCP `/n8n/capacity-ranker/campaign-state`. When it reports `all_running: false`, POST `/n8n/capacity-ranker/heal`.

**DETECT, THEN REPAIR.** Detection alone was not enough. On 2026-09-04 `Data - Warm Leads less than 30` sat NOT_RUNNING for roughly two hours after a reorder stopped it and the restart never succeeded (`dial_priority_log` id 24, `downtime_ms` 199717). Mark restarted it by hand; ~2,600 warm leads went undialed. The watchdog saw it and said so — nothing brought it back. `/heal` is that missing half: it restarts any campaign a failed cycle left NOT_RUNNING, verified.

**This workflow does not alert. LP-MCP does.** Both routes post their own GroupMe messages — the outage card from `campaign-state`, the healed / heal-failed outcome from `/heal`. `GROUPME_BOT_ID` is set on LP-MCP and on neither n8n service, and n8n runs with `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE` set, so an alert built here posted with no bot id and was rejected silently. The bot id stays on the LP-MCP side.

**`/heal` is idempotent.** It only ever STARTS a campaign, never stops one, and no-ops when everything is already RUNNING — so calling it on every unhealthy poll is safe.

**Activating this workflow IS the on switch** — nothing else calls these routes.

**Reading the executions:** a 200 all the way through is a healthy floor. A red execution means either the heal failed (503 — a campaign is STILL down, look now) or a route could not be reached (LP-MCP down — nobody was paged, look now).

nodes.name: GET campaign-state
nodes.notes: 200 = both Data campaigns RUNNING. 503 = one is not, and LP-MCP has already sent the GroupMe alert. neverError is set so a 503 REACHES the IF node below and triggers the heal instead of failing the execution on the spot — a transport failure (LP-MCP unreachable) still fails the execution, which is the signal that nobody was paged.

nodes.name: Any campaign down?
nodes.notes: Keyed on all_running — the LITERAL Five9 state — not on needs_attention, which is 200 while the ranker is mid-cycle. A campaign down because a cycle is in flight is healed to no effect; a campaign down because a cycle DIED is exactly what this exists for.

nodes.name: POST heal
nodes.notes: Restarts any campaign the last failed cycle left NOT_RUNNING, verified, and posts the outcome to GroupMe itself (healed / heal_failed). 200 = nothing left dark. 503 = a campaign is STILL down after the attempt, and the failed execution is the second signal. Idempotent: it only starts, never stops, and no-ops when everything is already RUNNING. 60s timeout because a verified start polls Five9 state, which reports on a 5-8s lag.

meta.note: Lives in n8n as workflow zIJSpafEg5Gwx2Mw, ACTIVE, published 2026-09-04 (version a02a2ff2). The heal branch requires LP-MCP to expose POST /n8n/capacity-ranker/heal, which shipped in LP-MCP#849. Mark enables CAPACITY_RANKER_CYCLE_CAMPAIGNS on LP-MCP only after /heal has been exercised against a deliberately stopped campaign.
